spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact imperative surfaces the explainer contrasts itself against: PerformanceObserver.observe({type, buffered:true}) vs observe({type}) for the four types in Chromium's declarative vocabulary (navigation, mark, visibility-state, largest-contentful-paint — verified against ParseEntryType in services/network/public/cpp/declarative_performance_observer_parser.cc), plus longtask as the documented not-in-vocabulary contrast. The early mark is a real performance.mark emitted from a head inline script; the declarative column is explicitly labelled as the documented contract, never a live readout, because the feature has no JS activation surface.

interactive.rationale: Three real controls: register-late-observers (creates ten real observers and drains via takeRecords), emit-mark (real performance.mark with detail), and a 120 ms busy loop generating a real longtask entry. Live per-type counts update from real observer deliveries; the buffered column recovered the head-emitted mark and navigation entry while the unbuffered column showed 0 (missed) — verified in headless Chromium DOM dump with autorun.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises a live comparison of buffered vs unbuffered late observers against browser-resident collection, which is exactly the rendered table.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers observer-only types (LCP and longtask excluded from getEntriesByType to avoid Chrome's deprecation warning — timeline column honestly says observer-only), unsupported types per-browser (rows degrade to an explicit 'not observable in this browser'/'unsupported' label), the LCP-stops-after-first-input race (called out in the legend), and the PerformanceObserver-missing fallback which reports a separate telemetry assert.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6594955352080384, the explainer use-cases anchor, and the performance-timeline observe()/buffered spec section.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables for colour; buttons override background and color together including the disabled state; missed/caught states use accent-rose/accent-emerald on paper backgrounds (AA on ivory/paper); table scrolls inside .race-wrap.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Desktop verified at 1280 wide (screenshot read: table, banner, buttons all legible, nothing clipped). Mobile verified at a true 360 CSS px layout via a same-origin 360px iframe measurement harness because headless new mode clamps windows to 500 px: documentElement.scrollWidth 345 == clientWidth 345 (no horizontal overflow) and a 360-wide rendered screenshot was read; buttons are min-height 44px native elements. No physical touch device was available; evidence is layout+keyboard, not touch.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for asynchronous state changes
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native controls with visible focus and announce async state changes through polite live regions rather than visual-only updates.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Status readout is a role=status aria-live=polite region updated on every action; controls are native buttons with :focus-visible outlines and disabled states; the results table uses real th scope semantics.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive form controls panel no horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Let wide content scroll in its own container and keep the page free of horizontal overflow with wrapping flex/grid and overflow-wrap on long tokens.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The comparison table lives in an overflow-x:auto wrapper with a min-width so it scrolls instead of squashing; controls flex-wrap; measured scrollWidth==clientWidth at 360 px.

guidanceConsulted.query: reliable page lifecycle telemetry beacon visibilitychange pagehide
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Session-long telemetry must not depend on unload-time JavaScript; prefer lifecycle-robust delivery.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The page's framing and the declarative column contrast JS-dependent observers with browser-process collection that survives renderer death, which is the guidance's failure mode made visible.

openQuestions.title: With autorun/registration during parse, the unbuffered observer still catches the navigation entry (it finalis
openQuestions.detail: With autorun/registration during parse, the unbuffered observer still catches the navigation entry (it finalises at load); the 'missed forever' story is strongest for the head-emitted mark and initial visibility-state entry. Should the demo also register from a genuinely late setTimeout to make the navigation row miss too?

openQuestions.title: End-to-end declarative activation (header served, flag on, report POSTed) has not been exercised anywhere in t
openQuestions.detail: End-to-end declarative activation (header served, flag on, report POSTed) has not been exercised anywhere in this feature's demos because this deployment cannot send the Performance-Observer header and no OT token exists for the origin. Revisit with a flag-enabled Canary + chrome-devtools-mcp and a header-sending test server once available.

summary: Live buffered-vs-unbuffered race over the exact declarative vocabulary with real entries; verified in headless Chromium at desktop and true-360px widths with zero console messages after removing a getEntriesByType deprecation warning for observer-only types.
